added_models.model: HBV-infected HepaRG cells and primary human hepatocytes (NAP at or after inoculation)

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5479567, open access; PLoS JATS XML checked). model_kind ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro value: PHH are primary human cells, HepaRG a differentiated human hepatoma line. Opener and comparison share a year because the first use of this system for the class is the comparison paper.
engagement.model: HBV-infected HepaRG cells and primary human hepatocytes (NAP at or after inoculation)
engagement.note: First human-cell use of the class: REP 2055, REP 2139 and REP 2165 added at or after HBV inoculation of HepaRG and PHH; HBsAg, HBeAg and HBV RNA read out.
engagement.short: NAPs tested in HepaRG and human hepatocytes
engagement.quote: In this study, we investigated the specific anti-HBV antiviral activity of NAPs in the HepaRG human hepatoma cell line and primary cultures of human hepatocytes.
engagement.judgement: Opens the human-cell track at its first admissible use (epub 2017-06-21). Separate track from the draft's HepG2.2.15/UNC7938 assay (Blanchet 2019): different cells, HBV infection rather than an integrated genome, no endosomal-release agent, and the opposite prediction. Separate from the duck primary-hepatocyte assay (different species and virus).

engagement.magnitude_basis: post-inoculation HBsAg secretion: no change in HepaRG or PHH at up to 5 uM REP 2055 or REP 2139 ('did not elicit any antiviral activity'), vs 2-7 log10 serum HBsAg decline in REP 101/REP 102 patients (Al-Mahtab 2016); and REP 2055 blocked entry much more efficiently than REP 2139 while the two were comparable in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5479567); the quote was checked against the PLoS JATS XML so the italic 'in vitro' is in place. The patient side is the sponsor's open-label REP 101/REP 102 series (Al-Mahtab 2016), cited by the source. The source attributes the post-entry failure to endosomal sequestration of naked oligonucleotides in culture, which Blanchet 2019 later bypassed with UNC7938 (the draft's hepg2215-hbsag-secretion track).
engagement.model: HBV-infected HepaRG cells and primary human hepatocytes (NAP at or after inoculation)
engagement.note: Human hepatocyte cultures blocked HBV entry but showed no post-inoculation effect on HBsAg and ranked REP 2055 far above REP 2139, against the comparable multilog HBsAg loss both gave patients.
engagement.short: Human hepatocytes miss the patient HBsAg block
engagement.quote: Importantly, the in vitro data presented here show that REP 2055 blocks HBV entry much more efficiently than REP 2139, while the antiviral activity for these two compounds is comparable in proof of concept clinical trials
engagement.reason: Failed to reproduce the patient HBsAg loss
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: the paper opens from the patient HBsAg clearance already published (Al-Mahtab 2016) and sets its own results against the proof-of-concept trials in two places (Results: 'While exhibiting a similar antiviral activity in proof of concept clinical trials, the in vitro ability of REP 2139 ... was significantly reduced as compared to REP 2055'; Discussion as quoted), so comparison_stated true. It failed on both counts the patients could test: no post-entry HBsAg effect in infected cells ('NAP treatment after viral inoculation did not elicit any antiviral activity', abstract) where patients lose 2-7 log10 HBsAg, and a REP 2055 >> REP 2139 entry ranking where the clinic saw comparable activity. A failed retrodiction is contra, never retro (decision 10). The entry block it did show has no patient counterpart (no prophylaxis trial), so it earns nothing. Only engagement is scored: the assay predicts nothing about off-treatment control (efficacy), exposure (dose) or harm (safety; neutral-red cytotoxicity only, no patient comparison stated). A failed model stays failed on its track; no later prospective prediction from this system has been tested.

added_models.model: Primary human hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells and PBMC cytokine-induction assay (uninfected)

safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5341074 via Europe PMC; published 2017-03-08). Liver cells from surgical resections, PBMC from healthy volunteers; REP 2006, REP 2055, REP 2139 and REP 2165 at 0.05-50 uM; qRT-PCR and ELISA for TNF, IL6, IL10 and interferon genes against TLR3/7/8/9 agonist controls. model_kind ex_vivo (human primary cells).
safety.model: Primary human hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells and PBMC cytokine-induction assay (uninfected)
safety.note: All three members dosed on human liver cells and PBMC: no inflammatory or interferon response in hepatocytes or LSEC; weak TNF/IL6 in Kupffer cells and PBMC, secretion only at 50 uM.
safety.short: Human liver cells: NAPs barely immunostimulatory
safety.quote: In primary isolated human hepatocytes and liver sinusoidal endothelial cells no significant inflammatory or antiviral responses were detected for any NAPs.
safety.judgement: Opens a human ex-vivo immune track for the platform harm of phosphorothioate oligonucleotides (innate immunostimulation), which these cells, unlike the draft's mouse and cynomolgus toxicology, can show directly. Separate track from heparg-phh-hbv-entry: uninfected cells, an immune readout and a different prediction. Opener and comparison share a year because the first use is the comparison paper.

safety.magnitude_basis: cytokine induction: weak TNF/IL6 only in Kupffer cells and PBMC, no interferon response, secretion only at 50 uM (about 5x cynomolgus Cmax) in the model, vs serum cytokine elevations in all REP 102 patients at therapeutic doses that did not track HBsAg decline, with no pro-inflammatory clinical effects reported (Al-Mahtab 2016)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5341074). The patient-side cytokine data the source cites are an EASL 2015 abstract (Stelma et al., J Hepatol 62:S567), not a peer-reviewed paper; the comparison is admissible only because the tier-1 source states it. Replicor-coauthored. The status is a judgement call: read at the biomarker level (cytokines rose in all patients where the cells said therapeutic exposure was too low) it is contra; read at the harm level (no pro-inflammatory clinical effect, as the cells predicted) it is retro. Scored retro + partial for consistency with the draft's cynomolgus safety entry, where host-immune events in infected patients that an uninfected system cannot show were not counted as a miss. Registry: REP 102 is NCT02646189 (first posted 2016-01-05, start 2011-08, no results posted; NCT02726789, start 2012-10, results 2019-05-08, is a second REP 2139-Ca + pegIFN Bangladeshi record and may also be REP 102); the comparison itself became public with the paper, so year stays 2017.
safety.model: Primary human hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells and PBMC cytokine-induction assay (uninfected)
safety.note: Built after the clinic: weak, supra-therapeutic-only cytokine induction in human liver cells and PBMC, set against REP 102 serum cytokine rises that did not track HBsAg loss and no clinical pro-inflammatory effects.
safety.short: Human cells reproduce weak immunostimulation, partly
safety.quote: Indeed, elevation of serum cytokines are observed in all patients receiving REP 2139 in the REP 102 protocol but these elevations are not correlated with a reduction in serum HBsAg.
safety.reason: Weak immunostimulation reproduced; cytokine rise under-called
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the paper takes the patient HBsAg clearance (Al-Mahtab 2016) and the REP 102 cytokine data (Stelma 2015) as known and sets its cells beside them in its own words ('persist and are not accompanied by pro-inflammatory effects in vivo or in human patients'; 'well before any immunostimulatory or pro-inflammatory activity would be predicted to occur based on pharmacokinetics in non-human primates and the weak pro-inflammatory and immunostimulatory properties of NAPs observed in this study'), so comparison_stated true. What the cells reproduced: weak pro-inflammatory (TNF, IL6) and no interferon induction, matching the absence of NAP-attributable pro-inflammatory harm in REP 101/102 and later REP 401 (Bazinet 2020, 'did not alter tolerability'). What they under-called: the exposure threshold (secretion only at 50 uM) against serum cytokine elevations in all REP 102 patients at therapeutic doses; the source resolves this by uncorrelation with HBsAg decline, a mechanism argument, so partial. Retro, never same (decision 10). Safety, not engagement: the readout is the platform harm of PS-oligonucleotides, not the class PD (HBsAg). No prospective prediction from this track has been tested since.

considered_not_added: ALG-010133 (Aligos STOPS; Phase 1 NCT04485663 halted 2022-01-06 for insufficient activity after in-vitro HBV cell-model predictions): not a member of this tile (members are REP 2055, REP 2139, REP 2165; class_programs 3), so it scores nowhere under decision 12 and no track is widened for it; the checker's rule question 7 stands.

DHBV-infected primary duck hepatocytes (Noordeen 2013 in vitro, doi 10.1128/AAC.01003-13, PMC3811297): abstract read; the paper compares NAPs with each other and with other viruses, and Guillot 2017 sets it beside the duck in vivo (model vs model), but no source puts its prediction beside patient results; an untested-only ex_vivo opener (first use 2013) is all it could carry, which step 3 excludes.

Roehl 2017 cynomolgus serum-calcium statement against the Bangladeshi REP 101/102 mineral-deficiency symptoms: a stated retrodiction, but on the existing cyno-mouse-pk-tox track (dose and safety cells already drafted), so it is a status question for that track (checker rule question 10), not a missing system.

Mathematical viral-kinetic models fitted to NAP-treated patients (Shekhtman 2020, doi 10.1038/s41598-020-64122-0, REP 2139-Ca monotherapy in 12 HBV/HDV patients; Hershkovich 2023, doi 10.1097/HC9.0000000000000205, and the 2024 HBV-RNA kinetics paper, doi 10.1016/j.antiviral.2024.106061, on REP 401): in-silico descriptions fitted to the patient data themselves, not a model whose prediction was then compared with patients, and not used to choose a dose; the 2020 model is also HBV/HDV co-infection.

HDV in-vitro infection model with NAPs (Beilstein 2018, doi 10.1128/JVI.01416-17): hepatitis D, a different disease from this tile (MONDO:0005366); any patient comparison would be against REP 301 HDV outcomes, so it belongs to an HDV context, not here.

DHBV-infected Pekin ducks with REP 2139 plus ETV/TDF (Quinet 2018, doi 10.1002/hep.29737) and the mouse/cynomolgus PK-toxicology (Roehl 2017): already tracked in the draft (dhbv-pekin-duck, cyno-mouse-pk-tox).

WHV woodchuck, HBV-transgenic mouse, human-liver chimeric mouse (Schoneweis 2018), HepG2.2.15/UNC7938 assay (Blanchet 2019, Boulon 2020) and the Aligos re-engineered duck (Debing 2024): already tracked in the draft.

safety, index 2 (Roehl 2017, cyno-mouse-pk-tox), field: track status in 2017; current: untested opener only, nothing follows until the 2020 same (index 3); supported: a 2017 retro entry inserted between index 2 and 3 (retrodiction true, comparison_stated true, source_calls_it partial, magnitude direction_only, registry_date 2016-01-05), quote verbatim from Roehl 2017 PMC5466589: "In the present study, the calcium levels with REP 2139 and REP 2165 after 6 months of exposure in cynomolgus monkeys showed no changes in serum calcium at doses exceeding those used clinically." The same discussion states the patient side: "No changes in serum calcium or magnesium levels were encountered in the patients in the Bangladeshi studies who were experiencing these side effects." Retro, not contra: the symptoms are attributed to endemic heavy-metal liberation an unexposed monkey could not show (decision 4). Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.omtn.2017.04.019. proposed_entry.magnitude_basis: serum calcium: unchanged in cynomolgus over 6 months at up to 9 mg/kg (doses exceeding clinical) vs unchanged serum calcium and magnesium in the Bangladeshi REP 101/102 patients who had mineral-loss/heavy-metal symptoms; no shared number
proposed_entry.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5466589, Europe PMC). Sponsor-authored (Replicor) comparison. The patient-side calcium statement cites Al-Mahtab 2016, whose abstract attributes hair loss, dysphagia and dysgeusia on REP 2139-Ca to endemic heavy-metal exposure and does not report calcium; Al-Mahtab full text could not be retrieved (Europe PMC 500). Status is a judgement call (checker rule question 10): on serum calcium the monkey reproduced the patients (retro); on the symptoms the monkey was silent, but the source attributes them to heavy-metal liberation from bone in a heavy-metal-endemic locale, which uninfected, unexposed monkeys could not show. Registry: REP 101 NCT02646163 and REP 102 NCT02646189, both first posted 2016-01-05, no results.
proposed_entry.note: Monkey serum calcium unchanged at doses exceeding clinical, set beside unchanged serum calcium and magnesium in Bangladeshi patients with mineral-loss symptoms; symptoms themselves not reproduced.
proposed_entry.short: Monkeys match patients' unchanged calcium, partly
proposed_entry.quote: In the present study, the calcium levels with REP 2139 and REP 2165 after 6 months of exposure in cynomolgus monkeys showed no changes in serum calcium at doses exceeding those used clinically.
proposed_entry.judgement: Retrodiction stated in the source's own words: the discussion takes the Bangladeshi REP 101/102 side effects (Al-Mahtab 2016) as known and sets the monkey calcium data beside them ('No changes in serum calcium or magnesium levels were encountered in the patients in the Bangladeshi studies who were experiencing these side effects'). The monkey reproduced the measured human datum (no serum calcium change), so retro, never same (decision 10). Partial, not contra: the symptoms (hair loss, dysphagia, dysgeusia) are attributed by the source to liberation of endemic heavy metals from bone, a harm an uninfected cynomolgus without heavy-metal load could not show (decision 4). The draft's REP 401 entry (2020) stays the track's first prospective test.
